exposure: reduction of AoP on maternal pushing
change in the angle of progression (AoP) on maternal pushing
outcome: duration of the first, second and active second stages of labor
admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: 469 nulliparous women with singleton pregnancy at term
finding: In nulliparous women at term before the onset of labor, narrower AoP at rest and on maximum Valsalva, reflecting fetal head engagement, is associated with a higher risk of Cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The increase in AoP from rest to Valsalva, reflecting more efficient maternal pushing, is associated with a shorter active second stage of labor.
